title: Extension of Flett's mean value theorem to improper derivatives
statement:
Let $f$ be a function on the interval $\langle a,b\rangle$ having a proper or improper derivative at each point. Assume that the tangents at the endpoints are parallel. **Flett's theorem extension.** There exists $\eta\in(a,b)$ such that Flett's mean value relation holds:

$$
f'(\eta)(\eta-a)=f(\eta)-f(a).
$$

The conjecture proposes that Flett's theorem remains valid when proper derivatives are replaced by proper or improper derivatives, motivated by examples involving the sign and arcsine functions. Whether the assertion holds under precisely these hypotheses is not established in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.5715

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).
source_name: Ondrej Hutník and Jana Molnárová, “Flett's mean value theorem: a survey”, arXiv:1309.5715 (2013).
